html:
The University of Tartu was founded in 1632 by King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden, then ruler of Estonia and Livonia. It is the oldest university in the Baltic states.

It closed during the wars with Russia and reopened in 1802 under the Russian tsar as a German-speaking university. In the 1800s it was one of the main universities of the Russian Empire for science. The naturalist Karl Ernst von Baer taught there.

In the second half of the 1800s Estonian students in Tartu led the national awakening, which gave rise to the Song Festival and the epic Kalevipoeg. After 1919 it became an Estonian-language university. Tartu is still the intellectual centre of Estonia.
